topics.title: Electric Circuits
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: DRAFT — Define electric current as the flow of charge and state its unit, the ampere (A).
DRAFT — State Ohm's law and apply V = I R to series and parallel circuits.
DRAFT — Build a simple d.c. circuit and predict how current, voltage and resistance change in series and parallel arrangements.

body.text: An electric current is a flow of electric charge. In a metal wire, the charge carriers are electrons. Current is measured in amperes (A), and it is the amount of charge passing a point each second.
Ohm's law relates the current through a resistor to the voltage across it and its resistance. Voltage is measured in volts (V) and resistance in ohms (Ω).

In a series circuit the same current flows through every component and the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances. In a parallel circuit the voltage across each branch is the same and the total current is the sum of the branch currents, so the combined resistance is smaller than any single branch.

Use the PhET Circuit Construction Kit below to drag a battery, wires and a bulb or resistor onto the workbench. Build both a series and a parallel circuit and watch how the current and voltage change. A voltmeter is connected across a component; an ammeter is connected in series with it.

quiz.prompt: Which instrument is connected in series with a component to measure the current through it?
quiz.explanation: An ammeter measures current and is connected in series so that the same current flows through it. A voltmeter measures voltage and is connected across (in parallel with) a component.

quiz.prompt: A resistor of 6 Ω has a current of 2 A flowing through it. What is the voltage across it?
quiz.explanation: Ohm's law: V = I R = 2 A × 6 Ω = 12 V.

quiz.prompt: Two 4 Ω resistors are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
quiz.explanation: In series, resistances add: R = R₁ + R₂ = 4 Ω + 4 Ω = 8 Ω.

quiz.prompt: Two 4 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance, in ohms? Round to one decimal place.
quiz.explanation: In parallel, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. The combined resistance is smaller than either single resistor.

quiz.prompt: Which statement is true for a parallel circuit compared with a series circuit using the same components and battery?

options.text: The total resistance is always larger
The current through each branch is always the same
The total current from the battery is the sum of the branch currents
The voltage across each branch is different

quiz.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is the same and the total current is the sum of the branch currents. The total resistance is smaller than any single branch.
